REQ-DESIGN-GOALS-AND-NON-GOALS.coverage_note: The design-goal requirement is a meta requirement whose dependencies now have modeled or enforced subsystem evidence across explicit capabilities, immutable base state, measured boot, local-first sync, identity-scoped networking, sandboxed task execution, resource scheduling, userspace drivers, compatibility containment, package lifecycle, recovery, UX surfaces, and session boot. It remains modeled because multiple dependent rows still rely on synthetic boot roots, in-process sync or transport models, harnessed platform telemetry, userspace-driver shims, and compositor-buffer UX rather than fully enforced platform invariants.

roadmap.focus: Keep the design-goal aggregate pinned to the weakest modeled dependencies while graduating boot/trust, sync, network, driver, resource, update, and UX rows to enforced evidence.
roadmap.graduation_proof: All requirements listed in the meta dependency set are enforced in the manifest, and the design-goals row can reference only those enforced subsystem proofs.

REQ-TASK-FIRST-UX.coverage_note: The booted compositor service path now starts a task through the native UX controller, binds the task's signed app component and UI surface, opens document, workspace, app-panel, and full-screen task views against a real booted workspace entry, and records task-flow transitions in the event ledger. It remains modeled because the proof still renders inspectable compositor buffers instead of driving a real user-facing shell.

roadmap.focus: Move the compositor-visible task orchestration proof into an interactive rendered shell.
roadmap.graduation_proof: A rendered shell test drives task creation, workspace/document opening, app-panel interaction, and full-screen task focus through compositor-visible controls and records the same task-flow events.

REQ-WINDOWS-AND-VIEWS.coverage_note: A booted compositor endpoint proof now opens every required view type, renders inspectable surface buffers with workspace, detail, modal, active-window, and UI-surface state, verifies switching and missing-window denial, and recovers the full window set from the compositor checkpoint. It remains modeled because those surfaces are buffer-rendered records rather than a real display path.

roadmap.focus: Back the compositor service records with a real display or inspectable framebuffer path.
roadmap.graduation_proof: A booted compositor display test renders document, workspace, app-panel, and full-screen task views through the display path and verifies switching, recovery, and permission-review state from visible output.

REQ-PERMISSION-UX.coverage_note: The booted compositor service path now shows permission-review cards through the compositor endpoint, including what the app wants, derived reasons, object scope, network path, requested locality, requested lease, and allow/deny decisions; the event ledger records both permission-review and permission-decision events for the task. It remains modeled because the surface is still an inspectable compositor buffer rather than an interactive rendered permission UI.

roadmap.focus: Move the compositor-buffer permission review into an interactive rendered review surface.
roadmap.graduation_proof: A rendered permission review test presents object scope, reason, lease, network path, locality, and allow/deny controls through the compositor display path and records the decisions through the policy path.

REQ-DRIVER-HOT-SWAP-AND-FAILURE-RECOVERY.coverage_note: Supervisor restart, hot-swap, diagnostics, ledger events, visible-impact notifications, driver-directory rebinding, and runtime activation observation are implemented for modeled userspace driver records. Hot-swap reports now preserve the runtime activation generation, DMA domain, exclusive claim, and brokered data-plane mode returned by the driver runtime; the proof still needs to run against booted userspace driver tasks and live device-broker state.

roadmap.focus: Move runtime-observed crash and hot-swap recovery from modeled driver runtime records into booted userspace driver tasks and live device-broker state.
roadmap.graduation_proof: A booted test crashes or replaces a userspace driver, preserves unaffected services, rebinds device authority, emits structured diagnostics, and proves no full-system reboot occurred.

REQ-BASE-OS-UPDATES.coverage_note: The immutable-base manager enforces signed read-only activation, rollback metadata, and a verified boot-selection record for the active signed base artifact; the smoke gate requires that selection after rollback. Complete base image replacement is still represented by native state and smoke markers rather than a freestanding boot selector.

roadmap.focus: Move verified immutable-base boot selection from native state and smoke markers into the freestanding boot selector for real base image artifacts.
roadmap.graduation_proof: A staged signed base image boots, health checks promote it atomically, a failed image rolls back before service use, and the smoke log verifies the active slot across reboot.

REQ-HEALTH-CHECKS.coverage_note: Health-check logic covers each required condition, and strict service-path mode now refuses storage, network, or UI success based only on supervisor state: storage must resolve and verify a concrete path, network must open/probe/close an overlay session, and UI must expose a visible compositor surface. A booted service-path proof now stages a candidate base image against the booted storage, sync/network, compositor, and supervisor graph, forces boot, core-service, storage, network, and UI failures independently, and verifies rollback leaves the previous active slot selected before a later healthy activation can promote the candidate. It remains modeled until the same strict probes execute as the freestanding post-activation path for real base image replacement.

roadmap.focus: Move the booted service-path post-activation health proof into the freestanding activation path for real base image artifacts.
roadmap.graduation_proof: A booted activation test fails each required health check independently and proves automatic rollback before the new image is considered active.

REQ-ZIGOS-USER-EXPERIENCE.coverage_note: The experience requirement now has implementation-backed models for clean install, reversible app and base updates, local-first sync, object/task permission review, compatibility containment, recovery actions, compositor-visible task flow, and event-ledger audit. It remains modeled because the journey is still assembled through native demo/service harnesses and compositor buffers rather than a complete interactive rendered shell, and uninstall/removal still needs user-visible service-path proof.

roadmap.focus: Replace the harnessed demo journey and compositor-buffer records with interactive shell flows, and add user-visible uninstall/removal proof.
roadmap.graduation_proof: End-to-end rendered-shell tests drive visible platform surfaces for install, uninstall/removal, reversible update, sync, permission review, containment denial, and recovery, with event-ledger proof for each flow.

REQ-ONE-SENTENCE-SUMMARY.coverage_note: The one-sentence summary now maps each named concept to subsystem implementation anchors: capability checks, local-first sync, device identity, immutable base state, versioned object storage, task isolation, identity-scoped networking, and accelerator scheduling. It remains modeled because local-first replication, identity-first networking, and resource scheduling still depend on in-process or provider-backed model paths rather than fully booted/live platform invariants.

roadmap.focus: Keep the summary aligned with the modeled subsystem evidence while moving local-first replication, identity-first networking, and accelerator scheduling onto real service or platform paths.
roadmap.graduation_proof: Every requirement named by the one-sentence summary is enforced, and this row contains only aggregate references to those enforced subsystem proofs.
